# Generated by make write-unverified. Give a clause a test rather than editing here: while the two
# disagree, make check-spec fails.
# Source: docs/specs/**/*.md, one line per clause, as path:CLAUSE-ID: heading.
# Withdrawn clauses carry no verified-by line at all and are not listed.
# No count is kept here. Two branches that each verify a clause both edit the count, so it conflicts
# where the lists themselves merge cleanly, and a count nothing reads is wrong quietly. Count the
# lines, or read the warnings check-spec prints.

docs/specs/background-sessions.md:BG-7: a question the session would ask is held until a person answers it
docs/specs/background-sessions.md:BG-8: the mode is fixed for the process, bypass is refused, and a rule that allows does not answer
docs/specs/background-sessions.md:BG-9: attaching draws the session as a foreground one, and detaching leaves it running
docs/specs/background-sessions.md:BG-10: a reply is the next prompt and answers nothing that was asked
docs/specs/background-sessions.md:BG-14: a background session in a git repository works in a checkout of its own
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-1: a plugin is installed only by a command a person types
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-2: `plugin.toml` names its parts, and a part it does not name is not installed
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-3: fetching a source is a network effect, and the host is put to the person before it happens
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-4: the install lists every part in full and asks once
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-5: a plugin installs at user scope, into one directory the person's own, and a workspace plugin is inert
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-6: a plugin carries no decision
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-7: installing a part does not approve it
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-8: a marketplace is an index naming sources and digests, and it installs nothing
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-9: update, remove and list work from the recorded source
docs/specs/plugins.md:PLUGIN-10: a plugin's text reaches a turn only as the part it is
docs/specs/references.md:REFER-5: a `repository` entry is fetched once, with the person's yes, into `~/.bravebot/references`
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-1: `--worktree` starts a fresh interactive session in a worktree made for it
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-2: a name is a label of ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, and decides no path
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-3: `--worktree` is refused where a delegate's checkout would be, and where a checkout would not be kept
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-4: a worktree is written, placed, labelled and ruled as a checkout is
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-5: the session works in the worktree as a delegate works in its checkout, and reads its sources from the project directory
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-6: the record is kept under the project directory and names the worktree
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-7: a resume returns to the worktree, and is refused where it cannot
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-8: a worktree is kept until the person removes it, and the sweep never takes one
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-9: a command that begins another session works where this says, and `/cd`, `/branch` and an apply to the worktree itself are refused
docs/specs/worktrees.md:WORKTREE-10: `--worktree` composes with no other way of starting a session
